title: Hedy Lamarr
passages: Hedy Lamarr was born Hedwig Kiesler on November 9, 1914, in Vienna, Austria, a city famous for its cozy coffee houses, waltz music and grand old theaters. As a young girl, she loved taking apart her music box to see how the tiny pieces worked together. She began acting as a teenager, and in 1937 she escaped an unhappy marriage and sailed to America. In Hollywood, she became one of the most GLAMOROUS film stars of her time. She appeared in about 30 movies, including "Algiers" in 1938 and "Samson and Delilah" in 1949.

During World War II, Lamarr wanted to help. Working with the COMPOSER George Antheil, she designed a way to guide radio-controlled TORPEDOES so that enemies could not block the signal. Their idea made the signal jump quickly between 88 radio channels, the same number as the keys on a piano. They received a PATENT in August 1942, but the navy did not use the idea until nearly 20 years later. Similar ideas later helped make Wi-Fi, GPS and Bluetooth possible. Lamarr died on January 19, 2000, in Florida, at age 85. In 2014, she was honored in the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
